All frequently asked questions

Nothing on this page matches that. Ask us, and the answer goes up here.

The basics

AI that does tasks for you, rather than only answering questions. You message it the way you would text a friend and it handles the job: the inbox, a reminder, a lookup. It answers ordinary questions too, the way any AI chat does. The difference is that it can go and do the thing.
None. Setting up an agent is answering a few questions about what it is for, and add-ons are written in plain words rather than code. If you want to know how any of it works underneath, we will go as deep as you like, and if you would rather not, nothing needs it.
You will understand it. That is the point of a guided session: we walk through what it can and cannot do, and why we make each choice, while you watch it happen on your own computer. You leave able to change it yourself. What a session involves →
It runs on your computer, on an AI account of your own, and it asks before it acts: email waits for your Send or a time you set, and a calendar change waits for your approval. Neither is a setting. How the other nine handle both →
You would not. Keep the apps you like. The difference is that they wait for you to check them: your car registration renewal sits in an email you skimmed three weeks ago. Your agent catches the deadline, puts it on your list, and messages you before it lapses.
Keep it. Most AI waits for you to bring it a task, then the job ends and whatever is left over is yours to remember. Archie runs on a schedule on your own computer and reaches you first. If your problem is a hard task, a work tool is the right call. If it is that small things keep slipping, that is this. Side by side →

Add-ons

They do not talk to each other. Each add-on does its one job and hands the result back, and your agent decides what goes to the next one, or calls several at once and puts what they send together.
Because “everything” is hundreds of unrelated jobs under one word. Separate add-ons let your agent reach for the right one rather than read past the tax rules and the flight booking to find your dinner recipe. You still get all of it.
Each add-on carries a short description of what it’s for. When you hand your agent a task, it scans those descriptions, picks the one that fits, and only then loads the full instructions. That’s why focused add-ons matter: clear, narrow descriptions make the right pick obvious.

Cost & billing

Three pieces. The discovery call is free, 30 minutes, no obligation. A guided session is $250 an hour, and a bigger setup takes more sessions rather than a higher rate. The Archie app is $30 a month or $299 a year at launch, bought separately from sessions. Every cost, in full →
Yes, in two ways, and neither asks for a card. Free credits for 14 days: $2 of Claude usage on our account, so those messages pass through our server, and email and text reading are off while we are paying. Or free on an AI account of your own, with no end date: the whole app at 20 jobs a day, starting again at midnight. How the free tier works →
No. The app is a separate plan: Personal is $30 a month or $299 a year, Business $99 a month or $999 a year at launch; guided sessions cover our time building your agent with you. They are priced separately because they are separate things, and a session is worth having whether or not you keep the app running afterwards.
Yes, on the app: email us within 14 days of first starting a plan and we refund it in full. After that you stop a plan yourself from the Account page, and it ends when the period you have paid for does. Guided sessions are hours already spent with you, so they are not refundable, which is part of why the call is free. What stopping looks like, step by step →
Yes, and for a personal agent it is small. You pay your AI company directly for what your agent does: $1 to $5 a month for a handful of tasks a day, $21 to $42 with a calendar and inbox connected, $64 to $139 for one wired into a whole working day. You can set a hard spending cap on their site. Where those figures come from →
A subscription works inside that company’s own app and cannot be used by a program you own. An AI account of your own can: you pay for what you use, often less than a subscription, with no daily cap, and your own subscription keeps working as normal. What each company does with what you send it is quoted on the Trust page.

Safety & privacy

Only the ones you approve. We go through everything with you before connecting anything, and you can revoke access at any time. Nothing gets linked without your explicit sign-off.
It drafts, you send. A text goes out only when you tap Send, an email when you send it or set a time, and a calendar change only after your next message says yes, never while you are away. Buying is off until you switch it on. Then it can place an order on a website, only at shops you pick and only up to the limits you set, and anything outside them comes back to you to press. It never types a card number, and the limit is checked against the price it reads on the page, so for a hard ceiling give it a card from your bank that works at one shop. What that looks like at a checkout → The honest limits on that gate →
A fair thing to ask about software you are about to give your calendar to. Your agent is in one conversation, the one with you, and it is not awake in between: three things start it, and nothing runs between them. It cannot run a program on your computer or make calls and texts, and it buys nothing unless you switched buying on. What none of that promises is that it will always be right, which is why everything that leaves your computer waits for you. What enforces each one →
We fix what can be fixed and tune the agent from your feedback. A sent message or an approved change may not be reversible, so review drafts and proposals before approving them. Early mistakes are why the tuning period and approval steps exist.
No. Your agent’s instructions, files, chat history and key all stay on your computer, and on an AI account of your own its thinking goes straight to that company. Free credits run through a server of ours, which measures spend without recording what was said. What we do hold is your email address, your plan and a handful of operational records, none of which holds anything you wrote. The whole list →
It lives in a folder on your computer, behind your own login and disk encryption, with your key in the system keychain rather than in a file. If the computer is lost, reset that key on the AI company’s site and disconnect the accounts. Nothing is copied to us, so restoring is yours to do, and Archie writes the file you would restore from, under Moving and backups. What travels and what does not →

Timeline & what to expect

A guided walkthrough is one hour. Larger builds are split into phases, with an estimated number of sessions and total cost given after the free discovery call. You can begin with one useful workflow and add accounts or jobs later.
Yes. This is the recommended path. Start with one or two high-value workflows, then add more once those are stable and saving you time.
Archie can work with connected email, calendars, files, chat apps and the add-ons in its public catalog. Common jobs include morning briefings, meeting preparation, research, reminders and drafting replies for your approval. Browse the current catalog or see how it works.
Tell us. We’ll scope it, quote it, and build the add-on. It’s yours, and it goes on the marketplace so the next person doesn’t have to ask. Commission an add-on to get started.
Once it is running it mostly looks after itself. The part worth your attention is not technical: it is deciding what to trust your agent with, and that goes as far as you want. We stay available either way, from a quick question to a working session, at no charge for anything we set up with you.

Practical details

No. You need a computer you are happy to leave on and connected; a Mac mini is the easy answer, never the requirement. Most people already own something that will do, and it spends most of its life idle, so it need not be fast or new. Answer a few questions and we will lay out your kit →
You stop a plan on Archie’s Account page, and it runs to the end of the period you paid for. On Personal, with your own AI key saved, Archie keeps opening after that: free, at 20 jobs a day. Every agent you made is still there and still works. Without a saved key, or on Archie for Business, it asks for a plan. Nothing on your computer is deleted in any of the three, and starting again restores access. Make your backup before you stop rather than after, since it is written from inside Archie. If we cease operations, our Terms require us to publish a final version with no license check within 30 days. All of it, in one place →
Whichever you already use. Archie works with Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix and, on a Mac, iMessage, and Telegram is the easiest to start with. You can also talk to your agent inside Archie: it is the same conversation either way, so there is no wrong pick and no rush to make one.
Any of the seven works and you can switch any time, so it is not a decision you can get wrong: tell your agent “use ChatGPT instead” and it does. Your agent does not change, because its skills, routines and memory sit on your computer. If you are unsure, Claude is a good default: it is what we build on and what the free credits run on. What each company does with your words →
Start on Balanced, and change it any time. Economy is quick and cheapest for simple work; Best uses the most capable model at a higher cost per message. If you are moving the dial to save money, know that an add-on can pick its own level and ignore it: the checkbox underneath is what overrides them. What that is worth, measured →
Yes to both: your agent runs on your computer rather than on ours, so it works while that computer is on, awake and connected. A laptop is fine, plugged in with sleep set to Never, and a cable from the router beats Wi-Fi because every drop is time your agent spends stopped. If it does stop, it picks up by itself when the computer comes back, with nothing for you to set up again.
